steps.context: Primary prior: CollecTRI human regulatory network, a signed literature-curated TF-target network (source/target/weight) delivered as a CSV that decoupler consumes directly. constraints: Python only; reading the DoRothEA .rda must happen through rpy2 inside the Python script, not via an R script
steps.description: Read the CollecTRI human regulon CSV and run decoupler ULM to infer per-sample TF activities on the T1S1 stabilized expression matrix; test each TF's activity difference aldosterone vs vehicle with padj correction. acceptance_criteria: Per-sample TF activity scores from ULM on the stabilized/log-normalized matrix for both priors saved as CSV, with n-targets per TF reported
Differential activity table per TF per prior: activity score difference, test statistic, p-value, FDR-adjusted padj, direction (activated/repressed in treated)
Agreement between CollecTRI-derived and DoRothEA-derived top TFs explicitly reported (e.g. overlap in the top 20 by padj)
TFs tested with fewer than a minimum number of regulon targets (e.g. 5) after intersecting with the 12,000-gene matrix are flagged or excluded, with the count reported
If the rpy2 load of dorothea_hs.rda fails, the step still completes with CollecTRI-only results and records the failure; it does not error out the run

steps.context: Reference gene sets staged under /mnt/refs: WikiPathways human 2026.07.10 GMT (HGNC symbols, '%'-delimited set descriptor to split) and MSigDB C3.tft GTRD TF-target GMT (506 sets named by the regulating TF's HGNC symbol; targets are ChIP-seq TSS-binding predictions with NO direction, so enrichment supports 'TF engaged', while sign interpretation comes only from the DE direction of the member targets). gseapy 1.3.1 is installed for pre-ranked GSEA.
steps.question: Do the DE statistics for aldosterone vs vehicle converge on coherent biological programs, and do independent TF-target gene-set collections (GTRD binding sets) nominate the same TFs as the regulon analysis?
steps.description: Pre-ranked GSEA (gseapy prerank) of the aldosterone-vs-vehicle DE ranking against the staged WikiPathways human GMT and the MSigDB C3 GTRD TF-target GMT, reporting enriched pathways and, for the TF-target sets, which TFs' bound targets are coordinately shifted — an independent, ChIP-based check on the T1S2 TF list.
acceptance_criteria: Preranked GSEA against WikiPathways human sets completed with per-set NES, p-value and FDR saved; sets filtered to a minimum gene overlap (e.g. 10) with the 12,000-gene matrix
GSEA over the MSigDB C3 GTRD TF-target sets completed the same way, yielding a TF-level list of enriched target sets
Per-TF GTRD result annotated with the direction evidence: fraction and count of the TF's bound targets that are up- vs down-regulated at padj<0.05
Ranked DE statistic used as input (shrunk LFC x -log10(p) or the Wald stat) documented; universe is the filtered gene set, not all genes
If a GMT is unreadable, the step completes with the other resource and records the gap

steps.name: Consensus ranking of TF drivers
caveats: Do not rank solely on p-value from one network; consensus means triangulation across priors and evidence types
A TF whose own mRNA is not DE can still be a driver (post-transcriptional regulation) — record DE status but do not use it as a filter
steps.context: Inputs: T1S2 differential TF-activity tables (CollecTRI primary, DoRothEA A-C robustness), T1S1 DE table, T1S3 GSEA outputs (WikiPathways programs, GTRD TF-target sets). No new reference data needed.
steps.question: Which TFs are the strongest, best-supported drivers of the aldosterone-treated vs vehicle response once regulon activity, TF-gene DE, and gene-set evidence are integrated?
steps.description: Integrate the T1S2 differential-activity results with T1S1 DE of the TF genes themselves and T1S3 gene-set support into a single consensus table of candidate TF drivers, ordered by combined evidence, flagging TFs supported by multiple independent lines vs single-source hits.
acceptance_criteria: One ranked table of candidate driver TFs with, per TF: CollecTRI activity score/padj and direction, DoRothEA A-C score/padj and direction, whether the TF gene itself is DE in T1S1, GTRD enrichment support, and supporting WikiPathways terms
Top TFs called out with direction of effect (activated or repressed in treated samples) and the evidence lines supporting each

A short caveats block stating: n=6 per group, unpaired, single batch; regulon networks are prior knowledge (CollecTRI curated, DoRothEA/GTRD partially predicted); TF activity is inferred, not measured
Explicit separation of high-confidence TFs (supported by >=2 independent evidence lines) from single-line candidates

plan.title: TF drivers of aldosterone response in kidney RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 human kidney genes across 12 samples (6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle, unpaired, single batch), with a 12x2 metadata table. The question asks which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-vehicle response. That needs three ingredients: (1) a statistically sound bulk differential-expression contrast on the counts, since TF activity is inferred from a treatment signal that must first be estimated (pydeseq2, Wald test, LFC shrinkage); (2) transcription-factor activity inference on the normalized signal and on the DE statistics using a signed, curated human TF-target regulon network (CollecTRI 2.0 CSV, staged under /mnt/refs) via decoupler's ULM method, with DoRothEA human A-C regulons loaded through rpy2 as a second, independent prior; and (3) orthogonal pathway-level support from pre-ranked enrichment against the staged WikiPathways human GMT and the MSigDB C3 GTRD TF-target sets, so the final TF ranking is triangulated rather than resting on one network. All steps are Python-only per the user constraint: CollecTRI is read as plain CSV, and DoRothEA's .rda is read through rpy2 from a Python script (with a declared fallback to CollecTRI-only results if that load fails). Small data (12000x12) keeps every step modest in resources; the two largest inputs (CollecTRI 4.3 MB, WikiPathways GMT 341 KB) are trivial to hold in memory.
